source.title: BLUEFIN: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Financial Spreadsheets

calls.rejected: concept 4 ("Krippendorff's alpha"): the alias "Krippendorff's Alpha" repeats its own name

candidates.name: rubric-based evaluation
candidates.summary: Evaluating complex outputs by checking them against a list of granular criteria, each with a point weight, and aggregating the points met into a score. It suits tasks too open-ended to verify with a single reference answer.
candidates.evidence: 3,225 granular rubric criteria

candidates.name: LLM-as-a-judge
candidates.summary: Using a language model to grade other outputs against criteria, often with tool access to inspect the artifact. Its reliability is usually checked by comparing its verdicts to human labels.
candidates.evidence: can be reliably evaluated by an LM judge agent

candidates.name: agentic evaluation harness
candidates.summary: The scaffolding that gives a language model agent a set of tools, a prompt and a loop for acting on a task, and records its trajectory so the result can be scored.
candidates.evidence: an agentic harness of 20 tools organized into six categories

candidates.name: Krippendorff's alpha
candidates.summary: A statistic measuring agreement among raters on labels, corrected for chance agreement. Values near 1 indicate high reliability.
candidates.evidence: we observed a Krippendorff's Alpha of 0.826

candidates.name: macro F1 score
candidates.summary: The F1 score (harmonic mean of precision and recall) computed per class and then averaged without weighting by class size.
candidates.evidence: GPT-5.4's macro F1 score of 0.839

candidates.name: perturbation testing
candidates.summary: Checking that a model's outputs respond correctly when an input is changed and the workbook is recalculated. It reveals hardcoded values or broken formula links.
candidates.evidence: A perturbation criterion specifies an input mutation

candidates.name: spreadsheet formula dependency
candidates.summary: Spreadsheet cells compute values via formulas that reference other cells, forming a dependency graph. Dynamic models use these links rather than hardcoded numbers so changes propagate.
candidates.evidence: dense, graph-structured dependencies

candidates.name: hardcoding
candidates.summary: Entering a computed number as a constant instead of a formula that derives it, which stops the value from updating when its inputs change.
candidates.evidence: Models that hardcode intermediate values

candidates.name: discounted cash flow analysis
candidates.summary: A valuation method that projects future cash flows and discounts them to present value using a rate such as WACC, adding a terminal value.
candidates.evidence: value the company using a DCF

candidates.name: weighted average cost of capital
candidates.summary: The blended required return on a firm's debt and equity financing, weighted by their proportions, used as the discount rate in valuation.
candidates.evidence: change WACC from 8.5% to 10%

candidates.name: financial modeling
candidates.summary: Building spreadsheet models of a company's finances, such as operating models, debt schedules, and balance sheets, to forecast results and support decisions.
candidates.evidence: building financial models from scratch

candidates.name: debt schedule
candidates.summary: A model section tracking debt tranches over time: balances, interest, amortization, cash sweeps, and revolver draws.
candidates.evidence: Build a debt schedule section at the bottom of the uploaded worksheet

candidates.name: circular reference
candidates.summary: A situation where formulas depend on each other cyclically, as when interest depends on a balance that depends on cash flow. Spreadsheets need iterative calculation to converge.
candidates.evidence: LBO-style circular references converge correctly

candidates.name: leveraged buyout model
candidates.summary: A financial model of acquiring a company largely with debt, tracking sources and uses of funds, debt paydown, and investor returns.
candidates.evidence: LBO-style circular references

candidates.name: Pareto frontier
candidates.summary: The set of options where no other option is both cheaper and better. Options off the frontier are dominated.
candidates.evidence: The Pareto frontier traces Grok 4.20 → Gemini 3.1 Pro → GPT-5.5

candidates.name: micro-averaging versus macro-averaging
candidates.summary: Micro-averaging pools all individual items before computing a metric, while macro-averaging computes it per group and averages the groups equally.
candidates.evidence: Overall micro (n=120)

candidates.name: benchmark data leakage
candidates.summary: Evaluation data leaking into training data inflates scores; keeping a private held-out set mitigates it.
candidates.evidence: We retain a private set primarily out of potential leakage concerns

candidates.name: sandboxed code execution
candidates.summary: Running model-written code in a restricted environment, with allow-listed builtins and imports and a timeout, to limit side effects.
candidates.evidence: restricted built-ins and a tight import whitelist

candidates.name: minimal-elicitation prompting
candidates.summary: Using a short system prompt with no workflow prescriptions so that results reflect the model's own capability rather than instruction-following.
candidates.evidence: we adopt a minimal-elicitation prompt (61 words

candidates.name: reasoning effort setting
candidates.summary: A model API parameter controlling how much internal reasoning the model does before answering, such as low, medium or high.
candidates.evidence: All models are set to high reasoning

candidates.name: human-expert annotation and review pipeline
candidates.summary: Collecting benchmark data through screened domain experts, with structured review and revision loops to enforce quality.
candidates.evidence: Reviewers worked through each submission against a structured checklist

resolutions.name: Krippendorff's alpha
resolutions.reason: Same statistic, Krippendorff's alpha, a chance-corrected agreement coefficient; the alias 'inter-annotator agreement' is the broader concept 29, not a match.

resolutions.name: macro F1 score
resolutions.reason: Macro F1 and macro-averaged F1 are the same metric, the per-class F1 averaged with equal weight.

resolutions.name: spreadsheet formula dependency
resolutions.reason: The dependency graph of cell references is related to hardcoding versus formulas but is a distinct idea, and it is not the same as circular references.

resolutions.name: hardcoding
resolutions.reason: Hardcoding is only one half of the existing contrast concept, which covers both hardcoding and formula-driven modeling, so it is a part rather than the same idea.

resolutions.name: discounted cash flow analysis
resolutions.reason: Discounted cash flow analysis and DCF valuation are the same valuation method.

resolutions.name: circular reference
resolutions.reason: Both define circular reference in spreadsheets, resolved by iterative calculation.

resolutions.name: Pareto frontier

concept.name: Pareto frontier of cost and performance

resolutions.reason: Both describe the Pareto frontier of cost versus performance with dominated options off the frontier.

shortlist.name: Pareto frontier of cost and performance

resolutions.name: micro-averaging versus macro-averaging
resolutions.reason: The contrast between micro and macro averaging is a broader concept that contains macro-averaged F1, which is only one application of it.

resolutions.name: benchmark data leakage
resolutions.reason: It merges contamination (existing 21) with the held-out set mitigation (existing 41), which are different concepts, so it is not the same as either one.

resolutions.name: human-expert annotation and review pipeline
resolutions.reason: Both describe building datasets via vetted experts with staged review and revision loops.
